Abstract
Kinetic proofreading limits the error ratio η of a discriminating enzyme; for a chain with n
proofreading stages the Hopfield limit is e−(n+1)∆ [1]. Whether the analogous bound holds for
arbitrary networks with two bound states is open. Published work gives bounds for specific
models or numerical Pareto fronts [2] [3], and a targeted search found no classification of this
family. With ∆ = ln 100, we prove η ≥ e−3∆ for the linear chain with n = 2 for all positive
rates and fuel potentials. Of the 88 admissible two-bound-state topologies, 50 obey η ≥ e−2∆
provably, 3 violate it with exact certificates (fam2_66: η = 5.082802e-07 at σ = 8.341626
kT per product, v = 1.4746e-03), and 35 remain open. The method combines symbolic
positivity proofs with exact rational reachability certificates. Main limitation: a single value
of ∆ and a bounded rate range, and 35 undecided topologies.

1

Introduction

Kinetic proofreading raises specificity beyond what free-energy differences or kinetic barriers
give, when the reaction is strongly but nonspecifically driven [1]. The ultimate accuracy of
such pathways is set by the displacement of the nucleoside triphosphates from equilibrium [4].
Several checking steps reach a given accuracy with less dissipation than a single one [4], and
more proofreading steps give better trade-offs [3].
Trade-offs between speed, error and dissipation have been studied analytically and numerically
through Pareto fronts [2] [3]. A dynamical phase transition has been reported in the mixed regime
[2]. A kinetically controlled bound on proofreading performance is determined by transition-state
energy differences [5] [6]. For Hopfield’s original network, scalings exist in which a speed-accuracydissipation ratio becomes asymptotically infinite [7]. Excessively strong discrimination can remove
the nonequilibrium advantage [8].
The open question: in the enumerated family of 88 topologies with two bound states,
can a fuel-driven discard exit bring η below e−2∆ ? The classification of this family and the
counterexamples were not found in a targeted literature search.
Contribution. We prove the chain bound η ≥ e−3∆ for n = 2 for all positive rates and fuel
potentials. We partition the 88 rule-conforming two-bound-state topologies into 50 with a proved
bound, 3 with an exact counterexample and 35 open. We give exactly certified topologies with
η < e−2∆ .
Summary of results.
• Theorem 1 shows η ≥ e−3∆ for the chain with n = 2, for all rates and fuel potentials.
• Theorem 2 shows η ≥ 1/D2 provably for 50 topologies of the family.
1

 • Theorem 3 gives the exact counterexample fam2_66 with η < e−2∆ .
• Theorem 4 gives two further certified counterexamples, fam2_9 and fam2_11.
• The classification theorem gives the full partition: 50 proved, 3 refuted, 35 open.
• Examples 1–4 give exact certified attainable points for the chain with n = 1 (numerical
optimisation, certified exactly).

Method

Certificate (a), exact reachability. Rates are rounded to rationals with denominator at most
106 and lie in [e−10 , e10 ]. Local detailed balance and the targets (η, σ, v) are then checked in
exact rational arithmetic. σ is reported as an enclosing interval. A numerical optimiser only
proposes candidates.

 Certificate (b), symbolic positivity. A bound η ≥ B is proved by writing η − B = N/D
as a ratio of polynomials in the rates and fuel factors, and checking that all coefficients are
nonnegative. This holds for all positive rates and all fuel potentials, independent of the rate
range.
Trusted base and numerical status. The trusted base is the verifier: the topology
generator, the exact certificate routines, and the rationalisation rule. The verifier passes its

5

Negative results

For 35 topologies, the bound η ≥ e−2∆ could be neither proved nor refuted by certificate. Further
failed attempts, including a question on the necessity of a fuel-driven discard exit and several
counter-checks, are recorded in Appendix A, because the corresponding claims are restricted to
the appendices.
4

 6

Discussion, limitations and open questions

The chain with n = 2 obeys η ≥ e−3∆ for all rates. Within the 88 enumerated two-bound-state
topologies, however, e−2∆ is not obeyed throughout: 50 topologies obey it provably, 3 violate
it with exact certificates, and 35 remain open. The counterexample fam2_66 has a fuel-driven
discard from the product state C1.
Limitations. The results hold for ∆ = ln 100, rates in [e−10 , e10 ], and the enumerated family
with one unbound state. The counterexamples are exact only at rationalised rates. The violating
points have finite dissipation and speed. The chain examples are attainable points, not proved
optima.
Open questions.
1. What is the status of the 35 open topologies: proved bound or counterexample?
2. Is a fuel-driven discard exit at the product state necessary for violating the bound e−2∆ in
this family?
3. What is the infimum of η for fam2_66, and how does it scale with ∆?

A

Agentic laboratory

Workflow. The laboratory ran 12 rounds with 11 verified statements and 1 negative result. Every
round was preregistered before the experiment. Preregistration H6 (commit 6184672) preceded
the first run, and addenda are dated. The L2c success criterion (at least 5 counterexamples in
one round) was missed: 2 in round 12, 3 in total.
Agents and roles. Four agent roles worked on the question on the necessity of a fuel-driven
discard exit: sparsam (haiku), numeriker (haiku), skeptiker (sonnet) and theoretiker (sonnet).
Negative result. For the question of whether going below e−2∆ requires a fuel-driven
discard exit at the product state, no claim passed the verifier. Every attempt (schranke_familie)
failed because of a verifier error that was fixed later.
Red-team statistics. Counter-checks in total: 22; passed: 4, did not pass: 8, not executable:
10. Selected outcomes:
• The symbolic proof of η ≥ 1.2 e−2∆ for the n = 1 chain failed, with 137 and 167 terms and
not all coefficients nonnegative, as expected for a false bound.
• The attempt to prove the bound for fam2_9, fam2_11 and fam2_13 failed for 0/3 members,
as expected for real counterexamples.
• A counter-check topology was rejected for violating the model rules.
• The reported non-smooth front was identified as an optimiser artefact, because the feasible
set grows with σmax .
Supplementary certified points. For hopfield_n1 with η ≤ 0.0004, σ ≤ 8 kT and
v ≥ 0.001, two certificates exist:
